QualityBucketRow.description: A bucket stored and recomputed side by side; `fields` name what differs (open, high, low, close, volume, bars) or `missing` / `unexpected`; `stored` or `recomputed` is null when there is none.

QualityBucketValues.description: The values of a bucket: open, high, low, close, volume and the number of 1-minute bars in it.

QualityBuckets.description:
The stored and the recomputed buckets of the window, computed when asked (`computedAt`), so they show the state now, whatever the last run saw. `total` and `differences` count all buckets of the
request's timeframe filter; `items` are cut at 2000 (`truncated`); with `differencesOnly` only the differing ones are listed.

QualityCheckResults.description: The checks of one instrument as the last run found them (without the long lists, which the detail gives separately).

QualityCheckStatuses.description: The status of each check of an instrument: pass · warning · fail · notAvailable (`officialDaily`).

QualityCounts.description:
The current results over the tracked instruments that have bars: how many there are (`tracked`), how many were `checked` (have a result), the counts by result, `notChecked`, and the mean score
of the results (null before the first run). The current result of an instrument is the one of the latest run that checked it.

QualityGateView.description:
The gate for the nightly plan (fail-closed). `blocked`: no run yet, the last run over every instrument failed, or more than `maxFailedPercent` of the checked instruments fail;
`ok`: not blocked and no instrument fails; `reasons` says why it is not ok. Instruments that fail individually are skipped by the scan whatever the gate says.

QualityInstrumentDetail.description:
One instrument's quality: the current result (`status` pass · warning · fail · notChecked, `score`, `checks` from the run `runId` at `checkedAt`), the missing minutes of that run
and the stored-vs-recomputed buckets as they are now.

QualityInstrumentRow.description:
An instrument in the quality table. `status`: pass · warning · fail · notChecked (never checked). `coverage` is the share of the expected minutes that are stored (percent); `aggregates` gives the status
of each timeframe (5m … 1M); `checks` the status of each check; `issues` says in words what is wrong; `source`: csv · dhan · mixed.

QualityMissing.description: The missing minutes of the window: `total` of them, and the first `items` (at most 500; `truncated` when there are more).

QualityOverview.description:
What the Data quality screen shows above the table: `lastRun` (the latest run over every instrument, null before the first), the `counts` of the current results with the mean `score`,
the `gate`, the `window`, the limits in force (`spikeMultiple`, `maxMissingPercent`) and `pendingCorporateActions`: the suggested splits and bonus issues waiting for the owner (ADR 0017 §5).

QualityPhase.description:
The quality phase of a data job (P1-14a): `Done` of `Total` are instruments checked. `RunId` is the quality run it recorded
(`/api/data/quality/runs`); `Passed`, `Warned` and `Failed` count the instruments by result so far. Part of the API (the job's
`quality` block, present only when the job asked for the step).

QualityRunView.description:
One run of the data quality checks. `trigger`: manual · daily (the scheduled end-of-day run) · after_job (a data job the owner started with the quality step). `status`: running · succeeded · failed.
`instruments` is how many the run checks, `passed`, `warned` and `failed` how many it has checked so far with that result; `score` is the mean (0–100, once it ended).
`instrumentId` is set when the run checked one instrument only (a fix action); `jobId` is the data job it belongs to.

QualityWindowView.description: The window of the checks: how many closed sessions, from which date to which (the ones a run started now would look at).

RefreshRunView.description: One refresh run. `trigger`: manual · daily · forced; `status`: running · succeeded · unchanged · failed; `phase` (while running): downloading · parsing · enriching · saving.

RefreshStarted.description: The refresh that was registered; follow it with `GET /api/instruments/refresh/status`.

RefreshStatusView.description: Where the master list stands: the refresh in progress (if any), the last finished one, the automatic schedule and how many instruments are active.

RemoveMembersInput.description: Instruments to remove from a basket (1 to 500; repeats count once).

RemoveMembersResult.description: What a removal did: `removed` were members, `notMembers` were not. Untracking never happens. `memberCount` = members now.

ResolveInput.description: Pasted tickers, canonical symbols (`NSE:RELIANCE`) or ISINs, up to 5,000 entries.

ResolveResult.description:
The outcome of looking up a pasted list. `entries` counts the non-blank entries, `duplicates` those collapsed because an earlier entry
was the same text or named the same instrument. Entries that match nothing are never guessed: they are listed in `unmatched`.

ResolvedInstrument.description: An entry that named an instrument. `term` is the entry as typed (the first one when several name the same instrument); `tracked` = tracked now; `retired` = cannot be newly tracked.

ReturnsView.description: The profit/loss figures that every holding row, lot row and summary carries.

RiskProfileInput.description: The values of a risk profile to create or to replace an existing one with. Every value is required.

RolesInput.description: Roles to switch; a role that is left out stays as it is.

SanityCheck.description: Bar sanity: low ≤ open and close ≤ high, prices positive and finite, volume not negative. `examples` holds the first few bad bars.

SchedulePreview.description: The dry run of a schedule: the findings (errors and warnings), the next three starts after now (empty when the schedule has errors or follows another service) and the schedule in words.

ScheduleSpec.description:
A Schedule as text: what the API sends and receives and what the database stores (JSON). `type` is daily · weekly · after · window · interval · continuous; times are
`HH:mm` India time; `days` are mon … sun; `weekday` is one of them; `after` is a service id. Fields that do not belong to the type are left out (null).

SecretStatusView.description: Whether one of the owner's Dhan secrets is stored (encrypted) and when it last changed. Name is the request field name ("apiKey", "apiSecret"). The value itself is never returned.

SecretsInput.description:
The Dhan API key and secret, write-only (app_id / app_secret). Surrounding spaces are
removed; the values are stored encrypted and never returned.

ServiceIssueView.description: A finding of the schedule checks. `severity`: error (blocks saving) · warning. `field` is a dotted path like the request (schedule.time, retries, parameters.x); `relatedServiceId` names the other service of a finding that involves two.

ServiceList.description: Every service: the registered ones in screen order, then the read-only entries.

ServiceNotice.description: A failure to tell the owner of (the bell). `id` is `service:failed:{serviceId}:{yyyy-MM-dd}` (the India date of the failed run): one notice per service per day, with the text and time of the latest failure. `kind` is service_failed; `severity` error.

ServiceRunPage.description: A page of runs, newest first. At most the latest int ServiceRunLimits.MaxShown runs of a service are shown; `total` counts those.

ServiceRunView.description: One run (or attempt) of a service. `trigger`: scheduled · catch_up · after · manual. `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped. `dataJobId` links the data job a run started.

ServiceScheduleInput.description:
The body of a schedule save or preview: everything the dialog sets, all of it required (a body that leaves a field out is a 400, so a missing switch is never read as "off"). `parameters` are the values by name
(those left out keep the schema's default); `revision` is the one read with the service (0 for a service that has no stored choices yet, also the default) and is only checked by a save.

ServiceView.description:
A service on the Services screen (ADR 0018). `status`: healthy · running · failed (its latest run failed) · paused. `schedule` is the stored form (`scheduleWords` says it in words);
`allowedScheduleTypes` are the types the owner may choose; `isDefault` says the choices are the definition's defaults; `lastRun` is the latest run of any kind, `nextRun` the next
scheduled start (null when paused, when it follows another service, is always up or has no day ahead). `revision` is sent back with a save (0 until the first save or seed). A `readOnly`
entry is set elsewhere (`manageUrl`) and refuses writes.

ServicesTimeline.description: The trading-day timeline: market hours (null on a day without a session), the review cutoff, whether the date is a trading day and every enabled service's starts and bands.

SessionCompleteness.description: One trading session of the window as completeness sees it: the minutes the calendar expects, the ones stored, and whether a refetch already proved the day unfillable (`bar_gaps`).

csrfToken.description: Must be sent as `X-CSRF-Token` on every state-changing request.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The session ends after this long without a request.

expiresAt.description: Absolute end of the session, whatever the activity.

elevatedUntil.description: End of the step-up window (password re-entered); null when the session is not elevated right now.

SessionInfo.description: What the client needs to know about its session.

SpikeCheck.description:
Spikes: a 1-minute move greater than `spikeMultiple` times the median move and greater than 1 %. One the next bar takes back (at least half) is a spike (a warning); one that is not
taken back is a `largeMove`, a real jump, only reported. `thresholdPercent` is the move a bar needed to count.

SpikeExample.description: A close-to-close move that was far above the median: `movePercent` is signed; `reversed` says the next bar took at least half of it back (a bad tick, not a real move).

StartDataJobRequest.description:
Starts a data job. `steps`: any of csv · dhan · aggregate · quality (default csv, dhan and aggregate; always run in that order); `forceCsv` loads CSV files again that were loaded already
and have not changed; `refetchGaps` makes the Dhan phase also retry the sessions it gave up on (status `unfillable`); `csvFiles` (at most 214 names from the CSV folder, only with the csv step) loads only
those files, still skipping the ones that are unchanged unless `forceCsv` — a name the folder does not have, or a list that is empty, is `data.invalid` (400).

StartQualityRunRequest.description: The body of "Run checks": the one instrument to check (null: every tracked instrument with bars).

StartRefreshRequest.description: Starts a refresh. `force` skips the "file unchanged" check.

elevatedUntil.description: End of the window in which sensitive actions are allowed.

SyncInput.description:
Body of "Sync now" (optional). Confirm: true applies an answer that would close all or most open holdings, which is otherwise refused with
`409 portfolio.confirmation_required` (the problem carries `listedHoldings`, `openHoldings` and `wouldClose`). With Confirm: true both
ExpectedOpenHoldings and ExpectedWouldClose are required (400 portfolio.invalid otherwise): the numbers the owner saw in the 409. If Dhan's answer differs
now, nothing is changed and the sync answers `409 portfolio.confirmation_stale` with the fresh numbers.

SyncRunView.description: A run of the holdings sync. Trigger "manual", "auto" or "import"; Status "running", "succeeded", "failed" or "skipped". Error is a short safe text.

SyncStatusView.description:
The refresh settings of an account and its latest run. Mode "off" or "daily"; NextRunAt is null when the mode is off. FirstImportDate is the date holdings
get when they are imported without a date of their own; HasHoldings is true once the account has any holding (the first import has happened). Running is
true while a sync or import of the account is in progress.

TimeframeCheck.description: The aggregates of one timeframe compared with the recomputed ones: `compared` buckets (stored or recomputed), `differences` among them.

TimeframeStat.description: A derived timeframe (`5m 10m 15m 30m 1h 1D 1W 1M`): the bars stored and the start of the newest one.

TimelineBand.description: A part of the day a service is up (`from`, `to` as `HH:mm`; a continuous service spans 00:00 to 24:00).

TimelineEntry.description:
What one enabled service does on the day. `kind`: mark (starts at the marks) · band (up over the band; an interval also gives `everyMinutes`). `followsServiceId` names the service a
run-after service waits for (its mark is the one of the service it follows, at the end of the chain).

TimelineMark.description: One start on the timeline: the India time as `HH:mm` and the instant.

TrackResult.description:
What a track call did (all counts are of distinct instruments): `added` never tracked before, `reactivated` tracked again after an
untrack, `alreadyTracked` nothing to do. `totalTracked` is the number tracked now.

TrackingInput.description: Instruments to track or untrack: 1 to 500 ids (duplicates are fine and count once).

TradeBadRow.description: A row that cannot be imported: the line of the file it starts on and why.

TradeBatchPage.description: One page of import batches, newest first.

TradeBatchView.description: One import of a file. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveTrades` counts its trades that are not voided and `Securities` the securities among them.

TradeCount.description: A number of securities and the number of trades of the file in them.

TradeFileSummary.description:
What was in the file. `Rows` are the data rows (empty lines do not count), `Parsed` the valid trade rows, `Duplicates` the valid rows that repeat a trade id of the file, `AlreadyImported` the trades of the file that are stored already
(and not voided), `NewTrades` the ones an import would store. `Bad` lists the first 200 bad rows (line, reason); `BadTotal` counts all of them.

TradeImportResult.description:
What an import did. `Batch` is null when the file had nothing new. `Imported` trades were stored, `AlreadyImported` were there already. With `Rebuilt` the lots of `HoldingsRebuilt` holdings were replaced
(`LotsReplaced` lots removed); `Report` is the preview the owner confirmed (statuses before the rebuild).

TradeNotRebuilt.description: A holding (or security) that an undo could not rebuild: its `Symbol`, the `HoldingId` when it is a single holding, and the `Reason` — `ambiguous` or the mismatch (`negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`, `fractional_after_adjustment`).

TradePage.description: One page of the trades of a holding, newest first, voided ones included.

TradePreviewReport.description:
The preview of a tradebook import — nothing is stored. `NotHeld`: securities the account does not hold now (their trades are stored by an import, not applied); `Unmatched`: those of them that are not even NSE shares or ETFs of the master list.
`Digest` fingerprints everything the preview shows (all securities, listed or not); an import with `rebuild` must send it back. `Securities` lists every security that is a holding or an NSE share/ETF of the
master list and at most int TradeCsvLimits.MaxListedUnmatched (200) of the unmatched ones; `SecuritiesTotal` counts all the securities of the file and `UnmatchedListed` the unmatched ones listed.

TradeRebuildView.description:
What rebuilding a holding's lots from its trades does. `Status`: `ok` (the lots would change), `unchanged`, `quantity_mismatch` (see `Reason`: `negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`,
`fractional_after_adjustment`; nothing is applied), `no_holding`, `ambiguous`. `Q` is the broker's quantity, `Net` bought minus sold (today's shares). `HandDatedLotsReplaced` counts the lots whose date the owner chose
and `SyncLotsReplaced` the lots a sync added, among the `LotsBefore` lots that an `ok` rebuild replaces by `LotsAfter` lots. `RealisedPnl` is the profit of the pieces the trades sold. `AdjustedFor` counts the corporate
actions that changed a trade. `Digest` fingerprints this rebuild. `OpenCostAfter` is what the open lots cost after the rebuild (Σ open quantity × unit cost; also for `unchanged`), `BrokerCost` the broker's `Q × A`
and `CostDelta` their difference. The open quantities always add up to `Q`. With no sales in the file and an opening lot (the file does not explain the whole holding) `CostDelta` is 0, to within the rounding of the opening
lot's unit cost to 4 decimals (0.0001 × its quantity); with sales — or without an opening lot — the first-in first-out cost basis of the trades can differ from the broker's average-cost figure (brokers keep the average by the
weighted-average-cost method, a sale does not change it), which is shown, not hidden. `CostNote` is `opening_cost_fallback` when the trades cost more than the broker's average cost allows and the opening lot therefore costs the
average cost. The four are null unless the trades fit (`ok` or `unchanged`).

TradeSecurityView.description: A security of the file: its trades in the file and, when the account holds it, what the rebuild would do. `Matched` is true when it is a holding of the account or an NSE share or ETF of the master list.

TradeSkipped.description: Rows of the file that were left out because they are not NSE equity trades: how many, and how many for each reason (`derivatives`, `commodity`, `currency`, `bse`, `non_equity`).

TradeUndoResult.description: What undoing a batch did — or, with `DryRun`, would do (nothing is changed then; `Applied` is false). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`). Holdings whose lots came from trades are rebuilt from the remaining trades; `NotRebuilt` lists those that could not be (a mismatch, or ambiguous) and keep their lots, `HoldingsNotRebuilt` counts them. An undo cannot bring back lots the owner dated by hand or a sync added that an earlier rebuild replaced: the holding returns to one default-dated lot of the broker's quantity and cost (or to the shape of the remaining trades); `HandDatedLotsReplaced` and `SyncLotsReplaced` count what the rebuild removes (the lots of the holdings it rebuilds).

TradeUploadForm.description:
The multipart form of the trade preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by TradeUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `File` the tradebook (CSV), `Rebuild` and `Digest` are
for the import: whether to rebuild the lots (default true) and the digest of the preview, which is required with a rebuild.

TradeView.description: A trade. `Side` is `buy` or `sell`, `Source` is `csv` or `manual`. A voided trade does not count.

TradingInput.description: The complete trading configuration (a replacement, not a patch); whether the role is on is changed with the roles. Mode is "paper" (default) or "manual_live"; CapitalSource is "fixed" (default) or "broker_funds"; Styles holds "intraday" and/or "swing"; allowed instruments: intraday EQ_MIS and FUT, swing buy EQ_CNC and FUT, swing sell FUT.

TradingRoleView.description: Trading role. Mode is "paper" or "manual_live"; Profile is the name of the risk profile (null when none is chosen).

TradingSettingsView.description: Trading configuration. Mode is "paper" or "manual_live", CapitalSource is "fixed" or "broker_funds", Styles holds "intraday" and/or "swing"; instruments are EQ_MIS, EQ_CNC or FUT.

TransferInput.description: Instruments (1 to 500) to copy or move from one basket to another; `mode` = copy · move.

TransferResult.description:
What a transfer did. Only instruments that are members of the source are transferred: the others are `notInSource` (for a repeated move, the ones
moved before). `added` became members of the target, `alreadyInTarget` were there already, `removed` left the source (a move only),
`newlyTracked` of the added ones were not tracked and are now.

UnmatchedEntry.description: An entry that named no instrument. `reason`: `not_found` · `ambiguous` (an ISIN of several instruments) · `invalid` (too long or with control characters).

UntrackResult.description: What an untrack call did: `untracked` were tracked, `notTracked` were not (nothing to do). `totalTracked` is the number tracked now.

UpdateCorporateActionRequest.description:
Changes an action and makes it applied (confirming a suggestion, bringing back an ignored one). Every field is optional and keeps its current value when left out (an empty body confirms as it is);
`note` left out keeps the note, an empty text clears it. `acknowledgeCsvAdjusted` as when adding: needed when the result is applied with an ex-date on or before `csvAdjustedThrough`.

UpdateSecretsInput.description:
Replaces the account's API key and/or secret (write-only). A value that is left out stays as it is; an empty one is invalid.
ApiKeyIssuedOn is the day the key was generated: it defaults to today when a new API key is given and can also be corrected on its own.
